regional_variants_part_2.name: Bulbasaur (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: The first stage of a Cryosys experiment to create a Pokémon resistant to both toxins and extreme cold. The natural bulb of a captured Bulbasaur was surgically replaced with a metallic 'Cryo-Core.' This bulb does not yet photosynthesize; instead, it draws geothermal energy from the ground. The Pokémon is confused and wary, caught between its natural instincts and the cold technology fused to its back.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Ivysaur (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: As it evolves, the Cryo-Core becomes more active, drawing more power and venting excess energy as frost that coats its metallic shell. The core begins to unfurl into sharp, metallic 'petals.' It is more aggressive than its Kanto counterpart, its natural instincts fighting against the cold, artificial energy growing within it.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Venusaur (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: The final stage of the experiment. The Cryo-Core fully activates, overriding the Steel properties of its casing. The metallic bulb bursts open, not with a flower, but with jagged, crystalline ice structures that constantly vent a supercooled gas, causing frost to creep down the vines on its body. It is a living fusion of nature and cryo-technology, a powerful but tragic Pokémon.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Squirtle (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: This variant of Squirtle has adapted to Aethel's iron-rich, rocky coastlines. Its shell has taken on a dark, basalt-like appearance, infused with metallic minerals that make it much tougher than its Kanto counterpart's. The water it shoots from its mouth is often gritty with sediment. It's a stubborn and defensive Pokémon, preferring to withdraw into its shell rather than retreat.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Wartortle (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: Its shell is now clearly metallic and has developed sharp, steely edges. Its ears and tail have taken on a more rigid, fin-like appearance, helping it to maneuver through the harsh coastal currents. It is highly territorial, using its durable shell to ram any perceived threats, including small boats that stray too close to its nesting grounds.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Blastoise (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: The ultimate coastal defender. The cannons on its back are now forged from solid, dark metal, capable of retracting fully into its armored shell. It doesn't just shoot water; it fires highly pressurized blasts of mineral-rich water that can scour rock and dent steel plating. When defending its territory, it anchors itself to coastal rock formations, becoming a living fortress.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Kingler (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: This variant is a grim testament to the region's pollution. Mutated by runoff from mining operations and Eon Remnants labs, its shell has fused with scrap metal from the riverbed, forming a larger, incredibly durable, and jagged carapace. Its massive pincer is misshapen, resembling a piece of rusted, broken machinery. It is a highly aggressive scavenger, thriving in environments too toxic for other Pokémon.
regional_variants_part_2.evolution: Evolves from Krabby in Aethel upon reaching Standard Rank while in a polluted water or urban habitat.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Graveler (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: Instead of growing larger and more jagged, this variant of Graveler has been smoothed over as if a millennia of powerful, geothermally heated currents acted on it. Its body is composed of dark, polished river stones, and its core is infused with heated water. It has fewer, more rounded arms and often lies perfectly still at the bottom of hot springs, making it easy to mistake for a simple boulder.
regional_variants_part_2.evolution: Evolves from Geodude in Aethel upon reaching Rookie Rank. Evolves into Aethelian Golem via trade.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Golem (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: The final form of Aethel's river-rock Pokémon. Its body is smooth and hydrodynamic, as if carved by millennia of powerful currents. The cracks in its stone body glow with intense heat from the superheated water within. Instead of exploding, it can vent this pressure through ports in its shell, creating a powerful, geyser-like blast of scalding water.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Turtwig (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: This hardy variant of Turtwig makes its home in the rocky alpine meadows of Aethel. Its shell is not soil, but a flat, durable piece of slate. The sapling on its back is a tough, windswept conifer that is resistant to frost and high winds. It moves slowly but is incredibly sturdy, often mistaken for a peculiar-looking rock by passing hikers.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Grotle (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: The slate on its back has grown into a larger, more protective shell, and the conifer on its back is now more developed. Small pebbles and hardy alpine mosses now cling to its body, and it sometimes allows smaller Pokémon to shelter on its back during storms, creating a small, mobile ecosystem.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Torterra (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: This Pokémon has become a true 'walking mountain.' Its back is a rugged landscape of jagged slate and hardy alpine conifers. It is incredibly slow but possesses immense defensive power and surprising physical strength, able to cause small earthquakes just by shifting its weight. It is a symbol of Aethel's enduring, ancient nature.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Chimchar (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: This variant of Chimchar is born from a chaotic fusion of science and magic. Its fur is a darker, more muted color, but the flame on its tail burns with an ethereal, pink-and-violet fey-fire. It is a hyperactive and mischievous trickster, using its disorienting flames and fairy magic to play tricks on other Pokémon and travelers.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Monferno (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: It becomes even more chaotic and unpredictable. The blue markings on its face and body now glow with a vibrant, pinkish fey light, and the fey-fire on its tail burns brighter. It uses its incredible speed and magical fire to confuse and outmaneuver opponents rather than overpower them with brute force.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Infernape (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: The crown of fire on its head now burns with an intense, magical, pink-and-violet fey-fire that seems to dance with a life of its own. It is a master of misdirection, using its blinding speed and disorienting flames to strike when least expected. It fights with an eerie, unpredictable grace, less like a martial artist and more like a chaotic dancer.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Fennekin (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: This variant of Fennekin has adapted to the profound magical energy of Aethel's aurora. Its fiery fur has become a shimmering, snow-white coat, and its large ears are attuned to the aurora's cosmic hum. Instead of eating twigs, it nibbles on enchanted icicles, absorbing their fey energy. It is a shy, graceful Pokémon that can weave small illusions from frost and light.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Braixen (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: It no longer needs to carry a twig, instead forming a sharp, magically-infused icicle from the moisture in the air. It has become more adept at weaving illusions from frost and light, often creating dazzling displays that mimic the aurora to confuse its opponents while it strikes with its ice-shard wand.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Delphox (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: A wise and powerful fey creature of the arctic, often called a 'Winter Sage.' Its fur resembles a robe of pure, freshly fallen snow. The icicle it wields has grown into a formidable staff, which it uses to channel the power of the aurora and command blizzards. It no longer sees the future in flames, but in the shimmering, shifting patterns of the northern lights.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Flabébé (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: Born during the long polar nights of Aethel, this variant of Flabébé cannot rely on flowers. Instead, it finds and bonds with a single, magically infused, unmelting snowflake. It draws energy from the cold air and the faint light of the aurora, and is almost never seen during the bright summer months.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Floette (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: The unmelting snowflake it carries has grown larger and more intricate, pulsing with a soft inner light. It flutters through snowstorms, tending to the frozen flora of the tundra and guiding lost Pokémon with its gentle glow.
regional_variants_part_2.evolution: Evolves into Aethelian Florges with a Shiny Stone.

regional_variants_part_2.name: Florges (Aethelian Form)
regional_variants_part_2.concept: It no longer holds the snowflake, but has fully merged with it. Its body is a beautiful, regal sculpture of ice and fey magic, resembling a queen of winter. It is said that its presence can gently lower the temperature of an entire area, bringing a peaceful, beautiful frost to the land. It commands the winter winds and is a powerful guardian of the most pristine, untouched corners of Aethel.
